- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model underperforms when sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per 3-day sentiment drop.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; apply 1–2% upward bias if sentiment remains bullish after day 15.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for each 3-day sentiment cycle shift.
